title: Real-Time Messaging Sequence
purpose: Show the complete Socket.IO real-time messaging lifecycle from connection setup through message send, delete, and disconnect
audience: Backend developers, frontend messaging UI developers, QA engineers
description: The real-time messaging system uses Socket.IO with JWT authentication on handshake. Users connect, join conversation rooms (via conversation ID), send messages through REST POST which triggers Socket.IO broadcast to the room, delete messages with broadcast of deletion event, and disconnect. Messages are persisted in PostgreSQL and broadcast in real-time to all conversation participants.

preconditions: User is registered and authenticated with valid Supabase JWT
Conversation between participants exists or can be created implicitly
Socket.IO server is running and accepting connections on configured port
Both sender and receiver have active status in profiles table
postconditions: Message is persisted in messages table with sender, receiver, and conversation references
All conversation room participants receive real-time new_message event
Deleted message has is_deleted flag set (soft-delete in DB, hard-delete broadcast to room)
Conversation last_message_at timestamp updated on send

nodes.label: Socket.IO Connection Init
nodes.description: Creator/Fan initiates Socket.IO connection with JWT token in handshake auth

nodes.label: JWT Token Verification
nodes.description: Socket.IO middleware validates JWT via supabase.auth.getUser() — rejects with auth error if invalid or expired

nodes.label: Check Token Validity
nodes.description: Evaluate if JWT token is valid, not expired, and corresponds to an existing Supabase auth user

nodes.label: Connection Rejected
nodes.description: Socket.IO connection rejected with authentication error — client must re-authenticate

nodes.label: Socket Connected
nodes.description: Client receives 'connected' acknowledgment from server; socket.data.userId set to authenticated user ID

nodes.label: emit join_conversation
nodes.description: Client emits join_conversation event with conversationId to join the room for real-time messaging

nodes.label: socket.join(conversation-{id})
nodes.description: Server adds socket to the conversation room; all subsequent events for this conversation will reach this client

nodes.label: Check Conversation Participants
nodes.description: Server verifies the requesting user is a participant of the conversation before allowing room join

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/messages
nodes.description: Sender sends message via REST API with receiverId and text/content to backend endpoint

nodes.label: Validate Message Request
nodes.description: Controller validates receiver_id required, text/content required, sender status must be active

nodes.label: Find or Create Conversation
nodes.description: Look up existing conversation by participants array; create new conversation if none exists (implicit creation on first message)

nodes.label: Verify Conversation Participation
nodes.description: Validate sender is a participant of the conversation; reject with 403 if not

nodes.label: INSERT into messages table
nodes.description: Persist message record with conversation_id, sender_id, receiver_id, text, content JSONB, is_read=false

nodes.label: Check DB Insert Success
nodes.description: Verify the message record was successfully created in PostgreSQL

nodes.label: Generate Signed URLs for Content
nodes.description: If message has content attachments, generate 1-hour signed URLs for thumbnail/images via StorageService

nodes.label: Emit new_message to Room
nodes.description: Socket.IO server emits new_message event with full message object to conversation-{id} room

nodes.label: Broadcast new_message
nodes.description: Creator receives new_message event; Fan receives new_message event; message appears in real-time in UI

nodes.label: DELETE /api/v1/messages/{messageId}
nodes.description: Sender requests deletion of owned message via REST API

nodes.label: Verify Message Ownership
nodes.description: Check that requesting user's ID matches message sender_id — reject with 403 if not owner

nodes.label: UPDATE messages SET is_deleted
nodes.description: Soft-delete message by setting is_deleted flag to true; preserves record for audit but hides from UI

nodes.label: Emit message_deleted to Room
nodes.description: Socket.IO server emits message_deleted event with messageId to conversation room

nodes.label: Broadcast message_deleted
nodes.description: All conversation participants receive deletion event and remove message from UI

nodes.label: emit leave_conversation
nodes.description: Client emits leave_conversation event with conversationId when navigating away from conversation

nodes.label: socket.leave(room)
nodes.description: Server removes socket from conversation room; client stops receiving events for this conversation

nodes.label: socket.disconnect()
nodes.description: Client disconnects from Socket.IO server; server cleans up socket references

nodes.label: Check if Receiver is Admin
nodes.description: After message send, check if receiver has admin role — if so, trigger support ticket sync

nodes.label: Append to Active Support Ticket
nodes.description: If receiver is admin, call support.service.appendUserMessageToActiveTicket() to sync message to ticket conversation JSONB

nodes.label: Handle Socket.IO Auth Error
nodes.description: If JWT verification fails on connection, Socket.IO emits auth error and connection is terminated

connections.label: JWT token sent in handshake auth
User navigates away or closes app
DB insert failed — skip broadcast, return error

decisions.condition: Is JWT token valid and not expired?
decisions.truePath: Proceed to connection acceptance; attach socket.data.userId
decisions.falsePath: Reject connection with auth error; client must re-authenticate

decisions.truePath: Generate signed URLs (if content attachments) and emit new_message to room
decisions.falsePath: Return 500 error to sender; do not broadcast

decisions.condition: Is the receiver an admin user?
decisions.truePath: Call support.service.appendUserMessageToActiveTicket() to sync message to active support ticket
decisions.falsePath: No additional sync — message delivery complete

decisions.condition: Does the requesting user own the message (sender_id match)?
decisions.falsePath: Return 403 Forbidden — only message sender can delete

errorPaths.destination: Socket.IO connection rejected with auth error
500 error returned to sender; no broadcast

errorPaths.trigger: R2 signed URL generation fails for content attachments
errorPaths.destination: Placeholder URL used; message still sent
errorPaths.recovery: Content attachment shown as placeholder; URL can be regenerated

errorPaths.destination: Message persisted but not delivered in real-time
errorPaths.recovery: Receiver fetches messages via REST GET on next page load — no offline queue

errorPaths.trigger: Support ticket append fails during message to admin
errorPaths.destination: Message sent but not synced to ticket
errorPaths.recovery: Error logged; admin can manually append to ticket

validationRules: receiver_id must be a valid UUID of an existing active user
text must be non-empty string OR content.contentId must be provided
Sender must have status = 'active' in profiles table
Voice message file must be under 10MB and audio MIME type
Message sender must be participant of the conversation
Only message sender can delete (sender_id match)
Mass message restricted to creator role (protectAndCreator middleware)
businessRules: Conversations are implicitly created on first message between two users
Conversation list is role-enriched: creators see fan totalSpent and isNewSubscriber; fans see creator profile
No E2EE — messages stored in plaintext in PostgreSQL
No offline message delivery — disconnected recipients must REST fetch
No typing indicators (typing/stop_typing events not implemented)
message_updated event registered on frontend but never emitted from backend (dead event)
securityConsiderations: JWT validated on every Socket.IO connection via supabase.auth.getUser() — remote API call
Messages stored in plaintext in PostgreSQL — no E2EE; platform can read all messages
Voice message URLs valid for 7 days — extended window for URL leakage
No rate limiting on message endpoints — vulnerable to message spam/abuse
Offline message loss — no delivery guarantee
PPV content previews use CSS blur-md only — easily bypassed via browser inspector
performanceConsiderations: Conversation list query has N+1 user lookups per conversation
No React Query/SWR on frontend — useState + useEffect re-fetches on mount
No caching layer for conversation or message data
Mass message iterates subscriber list synchronously (N+1 pattern)
Content attachment processing (signed URLs) per message adds latency
Socket.IO broadcast overhead per message scales with room size

annotations.label: No offline delivery
annotations.description: If recipient Socket.IO disconnected, messages not queued — must REST fetch

annotations.label: Dead event: message_updated
annotations.description: Frontend listeners registered but server never emits this event

annotations.label: Missing typing indicators

annotations.label: No cross-tab sync
annotations.description: Active sessions in other tabs not notified of messages read state
